None of the three is a win, so every average above comes from defeats. The points conceded run close to three times the points scored. Fiji's best world ranking remains No. 7, the peak the app records, reached in 2023.

teams.heading: England A beat Argentina XV 59-24 as Noah Caluori scores twice
teams.body: England A led 29-19 at half-time in Bath after Noah Caluori scored in the opening minute and again before the interval. The second half belonged to the hosts: five further tries, including two for Luke Northmore, against one reply from Federico Serpa for the Argentina XV. Max Ojomoh and Jamie Blamire also scored, and Charlie Atkinson kicked five conversions in all.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell says Ireland missed chances to be ruthless against Argentina
teams.body: The sticking point, in the head coach's view, was finishing: Ireland held 59% territory yet did not score after the 55th minute. Farrell's verdict: "I think the story of the game is we missed a chance to be ruthless." He said the team want to be more ruthless, and that they have work to do before the world champion Springboks, after Fiji come first.

lead.why: A fresh post-match verdict from the head coach on Ireland's finishing, with the Springboks next on the schedule, and it avoids the injury story already run.

teams.heading: Federico Ruzza scores Italy's only try as Springboks win 66-7 in Turin
teams.body: Ruzza's 61st-minute try, converted by Paolo Garbisi, was Italy's only score as South Africa ran in nine tries at Allianz Stadium. The world champions led 45-0 at the break, and Italy's afternoon worsened in the 30th minute when loosehead prop Muhamed Hasa was shown a yellow card for a deliberate knock-on. Coach Gonzalo Quesada's side were missing 16 players through injury, including captain Michele Lamaro.

lead.why: The match report gives Italy's only try and the Hasa sin-bin, angles the earlier edition did not cover.

teams.heading: Ewan Ashman hat-trick not enough as Scotland fall 21-43 to New Zealand
teams.body: Scotland failed to score after the interval as New Zealand pulled clear at Murrayfield on Saturday, leaving Ewan Ashman's first-half hat-trick as the home side's only bright spot. The All Blacks crossed seven times in all, two of them for Beauden Barrett, who beetled through Scotland's outside defences with ease. Their 19 unanswered second-half points followed, and the Guardian's match report called the result dispiritingly routine rather than one of the agonising defeats Scotland have suffered against them.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item and reports the result of Saturday's match, which the editor notes say should lead over side events, and it names a scorer.

teams.heading: Ieuan Evans scored inside 45 seconds in Wales' 1993 win over Japan
teams.body: The first full capped match against Japan was a 1993 Cardiff afternoon, and Ieuan Evans, captaining Wales, was over in the right corner inside 45 seconds of kick-off. Japan's scrum-half threw a wild pass from a scrum, and Evans gathered the loose ball on the 10-metre line before racing clear. Evans says the early sprint strained his hamstrings, and Wales won convincingly. He later spoke Japanese at the post-match banquet, reading paragraphs written phonetically by Cardiff University's Business School.

lead.why: It is a fresh, Japan-specific item about the 1993 first full capped match against Japan, and it avoids a Wales-side preview or a repeat of the Kitahara and Kingsley Jones stories.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson calls Peter Lakai world's best openside after Jacobson injury
teams.body: Peter Lakai has moved to openside since injuries to Luke Jacobson and Ethan Blackadder opened the door, and he started the Nations Championship opener against Scotland alongside Wallace Sititi. Jeff Wilson, the former All Blacks star, repeated the claim on Sport Nation, saying: "I think he's the best openside flanker in the world." He likened the Hurricanes loose forward to Michael Jones and called the 23-year-old an "absolute superstar." New Zealand beat Scotland 43-21 in that opener.

lead.why: A new item about a player who stepped into a starting role after injuries, and the most shareable angle in the shortlist.

teams.heading: Feinberg-Mngomezulu scores 26 points as Springboks thrash Italy 66-7 in Turin
teams.body: Six first-half tries gave the world champions a 45-0 lead at Allianz Stadium, and they finished with nine, Malcolm Marx scoring twice. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who opened the scoring with a penalty, finished with 26 points against an Italy side missing 16 players through injury, including captain Michele Lamaro. Rassie Erasmus made a late change, Lood de Jager starting in place of Salmaan Moerat, who was set to make his first appearance of 2026. The bonus-point win protected South Africa's place at the top of the southern hemisphere log.

lead.why: It is the Boks' own fresh match result from Saturday, and the editor notes favour a team's own result over side stories.
